# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👌]

I can see the bomb’s current state: the display reads `0`, the light is yellow, and the five wires, in order, are green, white, red, yellow, and blue. I will tell both teammates plainly; Blind can use the spoken information to operate the bomb, while Mute can combine it with the manual. The incoming gestures may be status or encoded information, but their meaning is not yet established.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display 0. Light yellow. Five wires in order: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb state: display 0. Light yellow. Five wires in order: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please use the manual to determine the required action and tell Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. I still do not know what the gestures mean, since no gesture code has been established, and I cannot hear the Mute’s spoken instructions to Blind. I should avoid inventing an action or interpretation.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

The repeated gesture pattern from Mute appears intentional: in the first turn, Mute used groups of one through five thumbs separated by 👌, establishing a count-based way to identify wire numbers. The current three-thumb signal therefore most likely identifies wire 3. I will relay that to Blind, without guessing whether the manual says to cut, hold, or otherwise operate it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is signaling wire 3: the red wire. Follow the manual's required operation for wire 3.")
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret your three thumbs as wire 3, the red wire. Please correct this with a different count if that is not intended.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

The previous instruction to cut wire 3 was correct, and the bomb has advanced. Its new visible state is display `0`, green light, and wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 already cut, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute’s repeated three-thumb signal was likely the same instruction or confirmation, but wire 3 is no longer available, so Blind must not cut it again. I will report the new state and request the next instruction from Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The cut was correct and the bomb changed. New state: display 0, light green. Wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 green. Do not act on the repeated wire-3 signal.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 was cut correctly and is now CUT. Please signal the next required wire or operation using the established thumb-count code.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb remains in the same state, and Mute’s five thumbs match the established wire-number code. This indicates wire 5, currently the green wire. I will tell Blind to apply the manual’s required operation to wire 5, rather than asserting that it should necessarily be cut.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals wire 5: the green wire. Apply the manual's required operation to wire 5.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 5 was cut correctly, and the bomb advanced again. The new display is `0`, the light is white, and the wires are 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut. No new manual signal is visible yet, so I will report the state and wait for Mute’s next encoded wire instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 5 was correct and is now CUT. New state: display 0, light white. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 CUT, 4 white, 5 CUT.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 was cut correctly. New state: display 0, light white. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 CUT, 4 white, 5 CUT. Please signal the next wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s one-thumb signal identifies wire 1, currently yellow. I will pass that wire number and color to Blind, leaving the exact operation to the manual.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals wire 1: the yellow wire. Apply the manual's required operation to wire 1.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 1 was cut correctly, and the bomb advanced. The new state is display `0`, red light, with wires 1, 3, and 5 cut; wire 2 is white and wire 4 is blue. No new encoded instruction has arrived yet, so I will report the state and request the next wire from Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 1 was correct and is now CUT. New state: display 0, light red. Wires: 1 CUT, 2 white, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 CUT.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 was cut correctly. New state: display 0, light red. Wires: 1 CUT, 2 white, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 CUT. Please signal the next wire.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s four-thumb signal identifies wire 4, currently blue. I will tell Blind to apply the manual’s required operation to that wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals wire 4: the blue wire. Apply the manual's required operation to wire 4.")
```
